why: In a BST preorder, the root comes first, then all keys smaller than it (its left subtree), then all larger keys (its right subtree). Rebuilding is a recursive split by that boundary, or one pass that gives each subtree an allowed value range.
hints: The first value is the root. Which of the following values belong to its left subtree?

Everything smaller than the root, up to the first larger value, is the left subtree; the rest is the right subtree. Recursing with an (low, high) bound lets you consume the array in one left-to-right pass.

Walk preorder with an index: build a node if the next value fits the current bounds, recurse left with (low, val) and right with (val, high). O(n) time. Then serialize in preorder with # for empty children.
pitfalls: Every missing child prints #, including both children of a leaf.
A fully skewed input (strictly decreasing) is 1,000 levels deep: raise the recursion limit or use an iterative stack.
Values can be negative, so do not use 0 or -1 as sentinels.
